title: Fast Days in the Middle Ages
hook: Over 130 days a year, meat was strictly illegal.

scenes.text: In medieval Europe, the church mandated fasting for nearly a third of the entire year.
scenes.imagePrompt: Gothic stone monastery courtyard on a foggy autumn morning. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos

scenes.text: During Lent, Advent, and every Friday, eating meat, dairy, or eggs was strictly forbidden.
scenes.imagePrompt: Long rustic wooden dining trestle in an empty stone refectory hall. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos

scenes.text: So people ate fish. Pickled herring, salted cod, and freshwater eel flooded every town market.
scenes.imagePrompt: Medieval open-air river fish market with wooden barrels and hanging dried fish. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos

scenes.text: Wealthy lords got creative, reclassifying beavers and barnacle geese as fish to skirt the rules.

scenes.text: Even almond milk was invented as a butter and cream substitute during fast days.
